answer: Neighborhood closure ratio. Each peer records which peers first relayed its messages; an identity whose relays consistently come from a single dense cluster, rather than spanning diverse regions, gets throttled. A pearl of verified relay history must accumulate across separate clusters before full bandwidth opens, and forging that spread costs a copper of real infrastructure in each region plus sustained latency. The raven problem—one operator spinning many cheap nodes—fails because cluster overlap is visible in relay paths, forcing attackers to rent genuinely dispersed hosts.
